title: Research: exact additive echoes with three dirty arrays at any depth (no new kappa)
body:
**Status: research note / exact recursive interface. No new kappa.**

For exact additive factor shears, recursive children can temporarily borrow ancestor input/output rows and restore them on return. A fixed pool of **three dirty length-L arrays** suffices for every ordered binary/ternary echo tree, at any depth, while the external input remains read-only at every prefix. Private leaf and control workspace is separately charged.

The 56-factor witness executes the same **1,568 leaf calls** as the pinned PR822 sibling allocator, while using **three dirty arrays instead of five**. The fully reserved allocator needs nine for this same tree. PR822's exact optimizer also returns 1,568 at cap five and rejects cap four. This is a comparison within stated echo and allocator classes, not a minimum over arbitrary programs.

The changed hypothesis matters: a completed child must be an **exact additive** shear independent of its incoming dirty pool. The package reproduces an eight-factor nonlinear failure: `[-7, -4, -1, 2, 5]` becomes `[-7, 23, 5, 2, 5]`, corrupting a helper. PR822 preserves its helpers. The new literal inverse still reverses the whole state, showing why reversibility alone does not establish the required restoration contract. Rounded leaves cannot be substituted without additional work.

### Cost and scope

The written all-tree induction covers ordered noncommuting factors, arbitrary dirty values, both directions and exact integer headroom. The literal backend bill includes source/coefficient access, every inverse call, scalar work and its cleanup, program metadata, address events and explicit head travel.

At L = 2 and a common sufficient width of 119 bits, all three allocators execute 6,272 scalar multiplies, 9,408 add/subtracts, 9,408 scalar zero assignments, 15,680 reads and 3,136 writes, plus four startup zero assignments. Four clean scalar work registers and all coefficient/program storage are separately priced. Dispatcher/address costs remain explicit backend parameters. There is no physical fixed-tape compiler, rounded restoration, runtime speedup or improved multiplication exponent claim. The inherited direct all-role call obstruction survives.

Only `research/linear-port-borrowing/` is added (15 files). Base: `2921874911956718fcaaaf9396fe8267b3cfa9f0`. OS-random seed: **56**, recursive interfaces. Selected PR942 and its conditional kappa `1661960547713947 / 1000000000000000000` are unchanged.

### Reproduce

Python 3.12 or newer; standard library only:

```sh
python3 -B research/linear-port-borrowing/verify.py
python3 -B research/linear-port-borrowing/test_package.py
```

Both print `PASS`. Evidence includes:

- All 861 ordered binary/ternary trees through seven factors; 1,752 exact free-module replays including larger fixtures through 64 factors and two-row binary comparisons.
- A separate noncommuting interpreter retaining independent symbols for every dirty input; product, restoration, literal inverse, protected input and prefix bounds checked.
- 120 exact dense matrix/layout replays, with separate literal and invoice accounting.
- Sixteen mathematical rejection controls, a failed old four-row capacity, the nonlinear boundary and 13 package corruption controls.
- Identical canonical receipts on CPython 3.14.4 and a relocated, read-only CPython 3.12.3 replay under `-O`; original Git-blob/source pins, selected-record integrity, staged whitespace and clean patch application checks pass.

Canonical receipt SHA-256: `db16953e908c215678dcb4ec7c18b22b74f8444ee73df89c444082865717ea7f`. No full repository cold replay or hosted CI success is claimed.

### Attribution and overlap

The exact PR822 implementation, proof and notice by **shhxera** are retained at `8c5e1b557f59bca29139c4c2dcc65edfb808372b`. Credit also remains with **androolloyd (PR673)** for the echo, **Sagar Thakrar (PR730)** for the ordered optimizer, **Chafik Boukhalfa (PR628)** and all retained predecessor contributors. The constant-register algebraic principle is classical: **Ben-Or and Cleve**, SIAM J. Comput. 1992, [doi:10.1137/0221006](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/0221006). No literature-priority claim is made.

PR982's output-borrowed fanout, PR997's signed batching and PR1012's hosted restoration deferral have different interfaces. The refreshed queue through PR1051 contained no competing exact-additive arbitrary-depth pool result. The reserved-tree bounds in PR784/887 and nonlinear interface in PR896 retain their stated hypotheses.

Prepared for bitplane with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in reasoning, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0; original attribution retained. No independent human or formal full-theorem review is claimed.
